Przedborz Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Przedbórz, Poland

Not demolished. Przedbórz, granted town rights before 1370, recorded Jewish settlement from the turn of the 15th-16th centuries; by 1921, 3,749 (63.7%) grew to 4,500 (of 7,000 total) by 1937-38. A January 1940 ghetto held about 4,600; its October 9, 1942 liquidation forced residents on foot to Radomsko, then Treblinka. Nine postwar returnees were murdered by Poles in the 1945-46 turn. This cemetery is first referenced in an ambiguous 1636 royal privilege, though its oldest confirmed matzevah (Tojwa, daughter of Arie Lejb, d. August 24, 1754) makes it one of the oldest preserved Jewish cemeteries in the Łódź Voivodeship. Notable burials include Jeszaja Weltfreid (d. 1831), a student of the Seer of Lublin, and his descendant Abraham Mojsze Weltfreid (d. 1918), student of Chaim Halbersztam of Sącz. Germans broke matzevot for street paving during WWII, with destruction continuing postwar. A 2011 excavation at a local school square uncovered about 90 complete tombstones and numerous fragments dated 1910-1935; Hersz Mejlech Huss led a partial fencing effort in 2015 with the Łódź Jewish Community.
